scenes.headline: How open LLMs are trading full attention away
scenes.sub: A viral chart, recounted from the configs
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Vesna! A viral chart says full attention has vanished from open models. I recounted it.

steps.say: August to November: zero percent used full attention throughout.
The post names no source, but the watermark does. It is Sebastian Raschka's gallery, a hundred and twenty-two hand-picked architectures.

scenes.title: Recount it from the config files

steps.say: So I read every config. On the gallery's own list, the chart reproduces exactly. The last bar has no grey: nothing all-full.

steps.caption: 167 releases, 35 since late August
steps.say: Widen the list to a hundred and sixty-seven releases, and the zero goes. Fourteen point three percent still use full attention in every layer.
Filter by size and you see where it went. Under forty billion parameters, four of eleven. Over three hundred billion, one of eighteen.

states.say: Thirty-five releases. Five all full, nineteen hybrids, eleven with no full layer at all.
But ask a different question. Which of them can still read every earlier token, in some layer? All thirty-five.

scenes.title: Five layer stacks, one cell per layer

steps.say: Here is how. One cell per layer. K2 Horizon: full attention all the way down.
Gemma four: five window layers, then one full one.

steps.term: Gated DeltaNet: the past folded into a fixed state
steps.say: Qwen: three layers that fold the past into a fixed state, then one full one.
Kimi K three, the same rhythm.
Then K three point one Pro put an indexer in front of those twenty-four full layers. They are still there. They stopped counting.
MiniMax did the same to its last three. Same backbone, new class.

steps.caption: Every strip is a real config, first layer to last
steps.say: Those were drawings. These are the real strips, from the article's widget. Red is full attention, purple is sparse with an indexer.
Why do it? Memory. Qwen at its full context keeps about seventeen gigabytes of cache. With every layer full, nearly sixty-nine.

steps.caption: MiniMax M3.1 Flash at 1M tokens
steps.say: Sparse attention is a different bargain. At a million tokens MiniMax keeps a hundred and forty-five gigabytes, more than plain attention would. What it saves is reads: sixteen point four.

scenes.text: Open models are not dropping global attention. They are putting an indexer, a window or a fixed state in front of it.
scenes.mark: putting an indexer, a window or a fixed state in front of it
scenes.say: Open models are not dropping global attention. They are putting an indexer, a window or a fixed state in front of it.

recap: The chart is Raschka's gallery, reproduced exactly
A wider list: 14.3% still all full
No full attention usually means an indexer
scenes.say: The chart is real, for its list. The zero is not. Thanks for watching!
